description: One scheme, moved once per change, agreed across every place it is written down. A version that disagrees with itself is worse than no version, because a support conversation starts from whichever copy the reporter happened to see.

gates.title: The Version Is CalVer
gates.rule: The version is a calendar version, not a semantic one. Every project here is a service that ships continuously rather than a library somebody depends on a major of, so the useful question is when a build is from, and CalVer answers it in the number itself.
gates.fix: Move the project onto CalVer with bump-version.py, which uses the project's own release tool where it has one.

gates.title: Every Copy Of The Version Agrees
gates.rule: package.json, public/release.json and the README badge carry the same version. Each is written by a different step, so they drift apart quietly and the application ends up reporting a version older than the manifest it shipped with.
gates.fix: bump-version.py brings all three into step. Never hand-edit one of them.

gates.title: The Version Moved For This Change
gates.rule: The version on this branch is strictly ahead of the one on develop. A change that lands without moving the version is a change nobody can point at afterwards.
gates.fix: bump-version.py, in the same commit as the change.

gates.title: The Project's Own Release Tool Moved It
gates.rule: Where a project has a release script, that script is what wrote the version. A hand-bump into a manifest a project has a tool for is exactly the drift VER-02 exists to catch, one step earlier.
gates.fix: Run bump-version.py, which delegates to the project's script when one exists.
